ModMetaData.name: ISORIM 3D Strike Framework
ModMetaData.author: ISORIM FPS team
ModMetaData.description:
[h2]0.6.11[/h2] Adds compact first-person weapon cards, an aircraft and vehicle weapon rail, and a cockpit status panel bound to K by default. Reload bars appear during loading. The minimaps mark projected explosive impacts. Enemy aircraft keep native jobs without re-entering ground job loops. Air handling defaults to 60% for both player and AI. Fire drains component durability and can be extinguished with foam. Path connectivity now updates each affected neighbor once per batch. Update both ISORIM mods together.
[h2]0.6.10[/h2] Large raids enter in flights of up to three at 12, 18, 24, 30 cells and higher as needed. Sixteen aircraft add layers at 36 and 42 cells. Each flight climbs back to its layer after strafing. The gallery shows entry, strafing, and a wreck on a second-floor plasteel deck.
[h2]0.6.9[/h2] AI fixed-wing aircraft turn tighter and pull out after their strafing passes. Large raids enter in flights of three at 12, 18 and 24 cells, then climb back to their assigned layer. The airborne 5.56 mm gun has a modest range and rate-of-fire increase. Armed scouts can turn to defend themselves. Aircraft hits flash at the actual 3D contact and direct anti-air rounds skip their own gunner. Wrecks stop on solid upper floors and crash damage stays on that floor. Air-raid warnings use a new mechanical siren. Update both ISORIM mods together.
[h2]0.6.8[/h2] A claimed damaged vehicle now enters your faction’s repair list and can be repaired through Vehicle Framework. When a hostile pilot is incapacitated, a helicopter attempts a vertical landing at its current position or a nearby clear spot. Fixed-wing aircraft at or below 15 cells above the surface glide and roll to a stop if the route is clear. Higher aircraft crash and leave a recoverable wreck. Intact aircraft can be claimed after stopping and wrecks after repair. Update both ISORIM FPS Control Bridge and ISORIM 3D Strike Framework for these changes.
[h2]0.6.7[/h2] Developer raids with 8 or more aircraft now stage arrivals along the selected edge in flights of up to three. Each flight shares an altitude and a strike plan, and its survivors continue that plan. Ground-attack crews commit to a strafing line or rocket area and update their aim after pulling out. Preset raids also offer 12 and 16 aircraft. Includes the five loadout presets for each of eight aircraft and the four new vehicle sites.
[h2]0.6.6[/h2] Developer actions now offer five raid presets for Frog, Toad, Mosquito, Warbird, Smuggler, Cherokee, Louie and Goliath. Choose recon/self-defense, economy, bombing, multirole or full loadout, then launch 1, 2, 4 or 8 aircraft. Chassis, weapons and loaded/reserve ammunition are weighted separately. Added ground vehicle patrols alongside the original supply depot and four new world-site missions. Intercept an armored convoy, decode enemy communications, destroy two fuel tanks, or extract a parts crate. Tested with and without Combat Extended.
[h2]0.6.4[/h2] Routine air raids carry machine guns up to 7.62 mm or 40 mm HE/airburst. Rockets and 20 mm cannons are reserved for harder or boss encounters. Eight VVE airframes use compatible hardpoint loadouts and raid costs. The single-seat Frog with one 5.56 mm gun costs 450 raid points. Unarmed scouts circle the colony for four game hours. A completed survey has an 80% chance to schedule a raid with a countdown and arrival direction. Supported airburst weapons offer a proximity-fuzed anti-air mode with shock and fragmentation.
[h1]0.6.0 aircraft compatibility — November 9, 2026[/h1] [list] [*]Unified the supported aircraft station and upgrade layouts across the tested aircraft fleet. [*]Fixed the parachute support reflection call for the current IsoRim optional-parameter signature, preventing the repeating Parameter count mismatch exception. [*]Preserves existing weapons, raids, salvage and animations. FPS direct control remains optional. [/list]
[h2]Previous release information[/h2] [h1]ISORIM 3D Strike Framework[/h1] Build, upgrade and fly native aircraft, conduct ground attacks and air combat, bail out with a parachute, rescue survivors and recover enemy aircraft. FPS cockpit and external control are optional; the framework also retains normal tactical play.
[h2]Aircraft, upgrades and combat[/h2] [list] [*]Choose supported native aircraft and install their frame, engine, wing, armor and weapon upgrades. Upgrade nodes follow each aircraft layout rather than a shared fixed coordinate sheet. [*]Fly and land in physical 3D space. Crew stations, passengers, fuel, aircraft status and native vehicle systems remain active. [*]Use supported guns, rockets, guided missiles and bombs against ground or air targets. Weapon support depends on the source vehicle and installed modules. [*]Enemy aircraft can appear through the framework's aerial encounter systems. Shooting them down can leave survivors, salvage or a recoverable airframe. [*]Bail out, descend with a parachute and recover crew. Rescue and recovery use the native map and floor surfaces. Current support queries accept IsoRim's optional-parameter signature. [*]Vanilla and Combat Extended projectile routes are supported through matching optional integrations; installing CE is not required for the framework itself. [/list]
[h2]Default controls with the matching FPS update[/h2] Select a supported, crewed friendly vehicle and enter its FPS control. Mouse front side button/P cycles supported views; mouse rear side button returns to god view. WASD drives or taxis. Mouse aims the pilot view. LMB fires the selected weapon; RMB uses its optic. Tab changes weapons, B changes supported single/burst/automatic modes, G fires the supported machine gun directly, and R requests reload in direct control. Space: takeoff/ascend. Rotorcraft/pods: Ctrl descends, double Left Ctrl requests landing. Fixed wing: Left Ctrl brakes; L requests automatic landing. Shift: fixed-wing afterburner. T: supported orbit/hover point command. In god view, select an airborne aircraft and right-click a point to issue its aerial order. Bindings can be changed; another mod or an existing saved binding may override a default.
[h2]Installation and package relationship[/h2] Required: Harmony, Vehicle Framework, Vanilla Vehicles Expanded, VVE - Upgrades, IsoRim Waylith and ISORIM Vehicles Models - Standalone. Install source mods and their own prerequisites separately. Install the matching FPS Control Bridge for direct flight, true-3D combat, raids and rescue. FPS is optional only for native upgrade/loadout use. CE is optional. Disable the old VTOL R1/R2/R3 prototype packages instead of loading duplicate definitions. Use one FPS assembly, fully restart after updates, and keep a save backup when changing a large mod list. Private exhibition helpers, test saves, raw videos and upstream DLLs are not bundled in this mod.
The cover is AI promotional artwork. The gallery contains actual in-game captures and player footage; GIF previews are short, silent excerpts of the supplied videos. Thanks to the upstream authors, artists and testers.
Optional direct-control partner: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3824599915]ISORIM FPS Control Bridge (CE&Vanilla)[/url].
